Tax Reconciliation

The Tax Reconciliation report provides a comprehensive view of your tax account movements and balances over specified periods.

This report helps you track how your tax liability changes through sales, purchases, payments, and other adjustments.

Report Structure

The report is organized by tax account, showing for each account:

• Opening balance - Your tax liability at the start of each period

• Payments - Direct tax payments made to tax authorities

• Receipts - Tax refunds received from tax authorities

• Other movements - Journal entries and other adjustments affecting the tax account

• Closing balance - Your tax liability at the end of each period

Tax Liability Movements

Below the closing balance, the report shows what created new tax liability during the period:

• Tax on sales - Tax collected from customers on your sales

• Tax on purchases - Tax paid to suppliers that can be claimed back

The total of these movements represents the net change in your tax liability for the period.

Understanding the Numbers

Positive amounts increase your tax liability (you owe more tax), while negative amounts reduce it.

Click on any amount to view the underlying transactions that make up that figure.

The report can be generated using either accrual basis or cash basis accounting methods, depending on your tax requirements.

To create or modify this report, see: Tax Reconciliation
